message.content:
`contenteditable` is **not** a strict boolean attribute – it accepts three string values: | Value | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `"true"` | The element is editable. | | `"false"` | The element is not editable. | | `"plaintext-only"` | The element is editable, but only plain text can be entered (no formatting). | So when you want the element to be editable but restrict it to plain‑text input, you should set the attribute exactly to: ```html
…
``` There is no “boolean string” conversion needed; `"plaintext-only"` itself is the valid value. If you were using a helper that expects a boolean (`"true"`/`"false"`), you would need to treat `"plaintext-only"` as a special case and keep it as is.
